name: Exon Skipping
therapeuticGoalDescription: Restore production of a functional protein by preventing inclusion of a disease-associated exon during pre-mRNA splicing.
molecularDefect: Mutations that disrupt the reading frame or introduce pathogenic exons, where skipping one or more exons can restore a functional transcript.
diseaseMechanism: Binding of a steric-blocking ASO masks splice-regulatory sequences (e.g., splice donor/acceptor sites or exonic splicing enhancers), preventing spliceosome recognition of the target exon and promoting its exclusion from the mature mRNA.
suitableVariantTypes: Frameshift mutations; nonsense mutations; splice-site variants; mutations in exons where exon removal restores the reading frame while maintaining protein function.
typicalDiseases: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD); selected inherited retinal dystrophies (investigational); other rare genetic disorders with frame-restorable mutations.
rnaTargetRegion: Exonic splicing enhancers (ESEs); splice donor sites; splice acceptor sites; intronic splice regulatory elements flanking the target exon.
transcriptRequirement: A transcript in which skipping the selected exon restores or preserves production of a functional protein.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs. Common chemistries include PMO (phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer) and 2′-O-methyl phosphorothioate (2′-OMe PS).
typicalLength: Approximately 20–30 nucleotides, depending on target exon and chemistry.
designRules: Literature synthesis: target validated splice-regulatory elements; preserve reading frame; avoid RNase H-activating chemistries; experimentally validate exon-skipping efficiency by RT-PCR and protein restoration assays.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Prefer accessible splice-regulatory regions within pre-mRNA; RNA accessibility may influence exon-skipping efficiency.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential unintended modulation of splicing in partially complementary transcripts; transcriptome-wide splice analysis is recommended.
advantages: Clinically validated mechanism; can restore endogenous protein production without genome editing; reversible and sequence-specific.
limitations: Applicable only when exon removal preserves protein function; patient-specific applicability depends on mutation location; repeated dosing required.
clinicalTrialExamples: Eteplirsen; Golodirsen; Casimersen; Viltolarsen; numerous investigational exon-skipping ASOs for DMD and other inherited disorders.

evidenceLevel.note: Multiple FDA-approved drugs and extensive clinical validation.

referencesSummary: Aartsma-Rus & Corey (2020); Chen et al. (2024); Lim et al. (2020); FDA prescribing information for Exondys 51, Vyondys 53, Amondys 45, and Viltepso.
